name: LTK5208
full_name: 2x7.9W Pulse-Controlled Class-D/AB Dual-Channel Stereo Audio Power Amplifier
description: LTKCHIP LTK5208 is a 3ohm-capable, 2x7.9W dual-channel stereo class-D audio power amplifier with a single-pin MODE control that switches the whole chip between filterless class-D operation (low EMI, no output LC filter needed) and class-AB operation (lowest noise/distortion, used when EMI is not a concern). A separate EN pin gives single-pin shutdown independent of MODE, so a host can power the chip fully off or switch operating class with two GPIOs (or none, both pins can be left floating/strapped for a fixed default mode). Includes a DRC (dynamic range control) block the datasheet credits with reducing clipping-related distortion at high output power versus similar parts, plus overtemperature and short-circuit protection. Targets battery-powered portable audio: bluetooth speakers, smart speakers, GPS/handheld game consoles, and portable PA/USB speaker docks.

pins.name: MODE
pins.description: class-AB/class-D mode select: logic high = class-AB, logic low = class-D, floating = class-D (default)

pins.name: BYPASS
pins.description: internal analog reference/bias node; decouple to GND with a bypass capacitor (per the datasheet's typical application, 1uF)

pins.name: EN
pins.description: chip enable/shutdown, active low (logic low = shut down, logic high = on); independent of MODE

pins.name: GND
pins.description: exposed thermal/ground pad on the package underside; power supply return and primary heat-sinking path, must be soldered to the PCB ground plane

ESOP-10.notes: Per LTKCHIP LTK5208 datasheet (Ver 1.3, Chinese-language only), page 2, pin diagram and pin function table. Pin numbering confirmed from the top-view package drawing; the datasheet's own pin table has an apparent typo relabeling pin 10 as 'OUTNR' a second time, but the package diagram clearly shows pin 10 as OUTNL -- followed the diagram per the position-first rule. Pin 11 (GND) is the exposed pad, called out separately in the bottom-view drawing, not one of the 10 gull-wing leads.

extra.output_power: 10% THD+N, VDD=7V: up to 2x7.9W into 3ohm+15uH; up to 2x6.6W into 4ohm+33uH
extra.protection: overtemperature, short-circuit, click/pop suppression on enable
extra.output_type: BTL (bridge-tied load); class-D is filterless (no output LC filter needed)
extra.mode_control: single pin (MODE) selects class-D vs class-AB for the whole chip; single pin (EN) is a separate full shutdown

typical_application: Small battery-powered stereo speaker products where switching between class-D (efficiency, low EMI, no filter) and class-AB (lowest noise/distortion) matters: bluetooth speakers, smart speakers, GPS units, portable game consoles, boombox/PA speakers, and USB speaker docks. Typical application circuit ties MODE and EN to host GPIOs (or straps them) and decouples PVDD with a bulk plus ceramic capacitor pair, BYPASS with a small ceramic cap to GND.
gotchas: outputs are bridge-tied (BTL): wire each speaker between OUTP and OUTN of a channel, never to ground

MODE and EN are two independent controls, not a shared enable: EN is the full chip shutdown (active low), MODE only chooses class-D vs class-AB while the chip is enabled -- floating MODE defaults to class-D, not off

pin 11 (GND) is the package's exposed thermal pad, not a 10th gull-wing lead; it must be soldered to the PCB ground/copper pour both for the return path and for heat dissipation, unlike the 10 numbered side leads

datasheet is Chinese-language only from a small manufacturer (LTKCHIP, Shenzhen); no English datasheet or public part-number cross-reference was found, treat availability/second-source risk accordingly
the datasheet's own pin-function table mislabels pin 10 as 'OUTNR' (duplicating pin 7's name) -- the package top-view diagram is unambiguous that pin 10 is OUTNL; this entry follows the diagram
